title: Understanding PCA
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It does this by transforming the original features into a new set of features called principal components. These components are linear combinations of the original features.

title: Linear Combinations in PCA
text: When we say that the latent features in PCA are linear combinations of the original features, it means each principal component is formed by multiplying each original feature by a coefficient and summing them up. This transformation helps in reducing the dimensionality of the data while preserving as much variance as possible.

title: True or False: PCA and Linear Combinations
text: The latent features constructed by PCA are linear combinations of the original features.
